experiment:atlas.summary_plain: One of the two general-purpose detectors at the LHC. It recorded the collisions in which the Higgs boson was found in 2012.
experiment:atlas.summary_technical: A 46 m long, 7000 t detector built around a 2 T solenoid and an air-core toroid muon spectrometer, reading out roughly 100 million channels at a 40 MHz bunch-crossing rate.

experiment:belle.summary_plain: The predecessor of Belle II at the KEKB collider, which shared the 2008 Nobel Prize's experimental confirmation of CP violation in B decays.
experiment:belle.summary_technical: Ran from 1999 to 2010 and accumulated 1041 fb⁻¹, establishing CP violation in the B meson system alongside BaBar.

experiment:belle-2.summary_plain: An electron–positron collider experiment in Japan studying rare decays of B mesons, where a deviation from prediction would point to new particles too heavy to make directly.
experiment:belle-2.summary_technical: A hermetic detector at SuperKEKB's interaction region, aiming at 50 ab⁻¹ — fifty times the Belle dataset — with a DEPFET pixel vertex detector 1.4 cm from the beam.

experiment:cms.summary_plain: The LHC's other general-purpose detector — an independent instrument built so that a discovery has to be seen twice.
experiment:cms.summary_technical: Compact and heavy: 14 000 t inside a 3.8 T superconducting solenoid, with an all-silicon tracker and a lead-tungstate crystal electromagnetic calorimeter.

experiment:dune.summary_plain: A neutrino beam fired 1285 km through the Earth from Illinois to a 40 kt liquid-argon detector under South Dakota, to find out whether neutrinos and antineutrinos behave differently.
experiment:dune.summary_technical: Four 17.5 kt liquid argon TPC modules at the 4850 ft level of SURF, exposed to a 1.2 MW wide-band beam from the Fermilab Main Injector, with a movable near detector complex on the Fermilab site.

experiment:icarus.summary_plain: A liquid argon detector first run under the Gran Sasso mountain, rebuilt at CERN and now the far detector of Fermilab's short-baseline programme.
experiment:icarus.summary_technical: 476 t of active liquid argon in two cryostats, searching for the excess of electron-neutrino-like events reported by LSND and MiniBooNE.

experiment:icecube.summary_plain: A cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice turned into a telescope, which found the first neutrinos arriving from outside our galaxy.
experiment:icecube.summary_technical: 5160 digital optical modules on 86 strings between 1450 m and 2450 m depth, with the denser DeepCore infill extending sensitivity down to about 10 GeV.

experiment:lz.summary_plain: Seven tonnes of liquid xenon a mile underground, waiting for a dark matter particle to bump into a xenon nucleus.
experiment:lz.summary_technical: A dual-phase xenon TPC with a 5.5 t fiducial mass, surrounded by a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector and a water tank, at the SURF Davis Campus.

experiment:nova.summary_plain: Two liquid-scintillator detectors 810 km apart, off the axis of Fermilab's NuMI beam, measuring how muon neutrinos turn into electron neutrinos.
experiment:nova.summary_technical: The 14 kt far detector at Ash River sits 14.6 mrad off the beam axis, which narrows the spectrum to about 2 GeV — close to the first oscillation maximum at this baseline.

experiment:sbnd.summary_plain: The near detector of Fermilab's short-baseline programme, 110 m from the Booster neutrino target.
experiment:sbnd.summary_technical: A 112 t active-mass liquid argon TPC that measures the unoscillated beam so that ICARUS, 600 m downstream, can be searched for a sterile-neutrino signal.

experiment:super-kamiokande.summary_plain: A 50 000 t tank of ultrapure water a kilometre inside a Japanese mine, watched by eleven thousand photomultipliers. In 1998 it showed that neutrinos have mass.
experiment:super-kamiokande.summary_technical: The inner detector holds 32 kt viewed by 11 129 50 cm PMTs; an outer veto shell rejects entering muons. Since 2020 the water has been loaded with gadolinium to tag neutrons.

experiment:t2k.summary_plain: A neutrino beam sent 295 km under Japan from Tokai to the Super-Kamiokande detector; the first experiment to see muon neutrinos turning into electron neutrinos.
experiment:t2k.summary_technical: A 2.5° off-axis 0.6 GeV beam from the J-PARC Main Ring, with the magnetised ND280 near detector 280 m downstream and the 50 kt Super-Kamiokande water Cherenkov detector as the far detector.

experiment:ua1.summary_plain: The CERN experiment that discovered the W and Z bosons in 1983 by watching protons and antiprotons annihilate inside the SPS.
experiment:ua1.summary_technical: A 2000 t dipole-magnet detector in an underground area of the SPS, with a 6 m central drift chamber and near-hermetic calorimetry — the first collider detector designed around missing transverse energy.

facility:amundsen-scott.summary_plain: The United States research station at the geographic South Pole, above the cubic kilometre of ice instrumented by IceCube.
facility:amundsen-scott.summary_technical: Continuously occupied since 1956, at 2835 m elevation on the polar plateau. The ice below is exceptionally clear and free of radioactivity, which is what makes it a detector.

facility:cern.summary_plain: The world's largest particle physics laboratory, straddling the Swiss–French border outside Geneva. Its accelerator complex ends in the 27 km Large Hadron Collider.
facility:cern.summary_technical: Founded in 1954 by twelve European states. The injector chain (Linac 4 → PSB → PS → SPS) feeds the LHC at 450 GeV; the SPS also serves the North Area fixed-target programme and, from 1981 to 1990, ran as the SppS proton–antiproton collider.

facility:fermilab.summary_plain: The United States' dedicated particle physics laboratory, west of Chicago, and the host of the country's long-baseline neutrino programme.
facility:fermilab.summary_technical: The Main Injector delivers 120 GeV protons to the NuMI and (from the 2030s) LBNF targets; the 8 GeV Booster feeds the Short-Baseline Neutrino programme. The Tevatron ran here from 1983 until 2011.

facility:j-parc.summary_plain: A proton accelerator complex on the Pacific coast at Tokai, Japan, whose neutrino beam is aimed 295 km across the country at Super-Kamiokande.
facility:j-parc.summary_technical: The 30 GeV Main Ring delivers up to 760 kW to the neutrino target station; the beam is produced 2.5° off the axis to Kamioka, narrowing its energy spectrum around the oscillation maximum.

facility:kamioka-observatory.summary_plain: A cluster of experiments inside the Mozumi mine under Mount Ikeno, Japan — the home of Super-Kamiokande.
facility:kamioka-observatory.summary_technical: Roughly 1000 m of rock (2700 m.w.e.) above the Super-Kamiokande cavern. The site also hosts KamLAND, XMASS and the KAGRA gravitational-wave interferometer.

facility:kek.summary_plain: Japan's high energy accelerator laboratory in Tsukuba, home of the SuperKEKB electron–positron collider.
facility:kek.summary_technical: SuperKEKB collides 7 GeV electrons with 4 GeV positrons at the Υ(4S) resonance, with a nano-beam scheme designed for 40 times KEKB's peak luminosity.

facility:surf.summary_plain: A laboratory 1478 m underground in a former gold mine in Lead, South Dakota, where the rock above shields detectors from cosmic rays.
facility:surf.summary_technical: 4300 m.w.e. of overburden at the 4850 ft level. The Davis Campus hosts LZ and MAJORANA; new caverns excavated from 2021 will hold the DUNE far detector modules.

result:belle-2-first-collisions-2018.summary_plain: SuperKEKB delivered the first electron–positron collisions to the Belle II detector.

result:higgs-boson-observation-2012.summary_plain: We observe an excess of events at m_H ≈ 126.5 GeV with a local significance of 5.9 standard deviations.
result:higgs-boson-observation-2012.why_it_matters: It completed the Standard Model's particle content and confirmed that the mechanism giving mass to the W and Z is a physical field with a quantum.

result:icecube-astrophysical-neutrinos-2.summary_plain: These data provide evidence for high-energy extraterrestrial neutrinos at the 4σ level.
result:icecube-astrophysical-neutrinos-2.why_it_matters: It opened neutrino astronomy above a TeV: the universe has sources violent enough to send us particles that ignore everything in between.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-2018.summary_plain: We find evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056 at the 3σ level.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-2018.why_it_matters: It tied a single high-energy neutrino to a flaring blazar, the first identification of a source of cosmic-ray acceleration outside the galaxy.

result:lz-wimp-limit-2024.summary_plain: We set an upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP–nucleon cross section of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 40 GeV/c².
result:lz-wimp-limit-2024.why_it_matters: Each order of magnitude of cross-section excluded closes off a large region of well-motivated dark-matter parameter space.

result:nova-electron-neutrino-appearance.summary_plain: We report the first measurement of ν_e appearance in the NOvA experiment.

result:protodune-beam-test-2018.summary_plain: The ProtoDUNE single-phase detector recorded its first particle tracks from the CERN test beam.

result:super-k-atmospheric-oscillation-1.summary_plain: We present an analysis of these data which gives evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos.
result:super-k-atmospheric-oscillation-1.why_it_matters: It was the first solid evidence that neutrinos have mass — the first laboratory result the Standard Model could not accommodate.

result:super-k-gadolinium-loading-2020.summary_plain: Gadolinium sulphate was dissolved into the Super-Kamiokande tank to enable neutron tagging.

result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.summary_plain: The observed value of 28 candidate events excludes the no-appearance hypothesis at 7.3 standard deviations.
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.why_it_matters: Appearance of a neutrino flavour that was not in the beam opened the door to comparing neutrinos with antineutrinos, which is how leptonic CP violation will be measured.

result:w-and-z-boson-discovery-1983.summary_plain: The events are consistent with the discovery of the intermediate vector boson W.
result:w-and-z-boson-discovery-1983.why_it_matters: The W and Z are the carriers of the weak force. Finding them at the predicted masses confirmed the unification of the weak and electromagnetic interactions.

topic:higgs-boson.overview: The Higgs field gives mass to the W, the Z and every fermion. Measuring its couplings is how we test whether the mechanism is exactly the one the Standard Model wrote down.

topic:leptonic-cp-violation.overview: If neutrinos oscillate at a different rate from antineutrinos, the early universe had a way to end up with more matter than antimatter.

topic:neutrino-astronomy.overview: Neutrinos travel from the far universe in a straight line through everything. They point back at whatever accelerated them.

topic:neutrino-oscillations.overview: Neutrinos are produced as one of three types and arrive as another. That is only possible if they have mass — which the Standard Model said they did not.

topic:wimp-direct-detection.overview: Dark matter outweighs ordinary matter five to one. Direct-detection experiments wait, underground and very quietly, for one particle of it to hit a nucleus.
